title: InfSplign: Inference-Time Spatial Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
property: spatial relation, object presence and balance between two objects
reads: Cross-attention maps of the two object tokens from U-Net decoder blocks 1 and 2 (layers 1 to 3 of each), reduced to centroids and variances
trained_on: nothing trained; hand-written loss of centroid margin, attention variance and variance balance, weights chosen by grid search on a VISOR subset
gradient_enters: Added to the CFG noise prediction as eta times grad_z L, eta 1000, on all reverse steps of 50, one gradient per step, no stated cap
unseen: no: nothing is trained, and the weights are tuned on a VISOR subset covering all objects, then scored on full VISOR
headline: VISOR uncond (% of images with correct relation, higher better): 76.26 on SD 2.1 against 30.25 for plain SD and 62.06 for best baseline CoMPaSS; 78.44 on SDXL against 45.10 with no loss, with no other method compared on SDXL
copy_or_avoid: Use its centroid-margin loss as the untrained baseline on SDXL, and do not read our 0-of-8 anti-correlation result as showing attention losses cannot move SDXL (inferred)
model: SD1.4 / SD2.1, SDXL in one appendix ablation table

quotes.text: For coarse attention and mid-level attention, we use the cross-attention layers 1−3 of the first and second blocks of the U-Net decoder
we extract attention maps from coarse- and mid-level decoder layers of the U-Net
We introduce InfSplign, a training-free inference-time method
LInfSplign = λs Lspatial + λp Lpresence + λb Lbalance
Hyperparameters are selected via grid search
This is applied iteratively over all reverse timesteps.
provides a guidance signal that modifies the predicted noise
the guidance weight for our loss is set to η = 1000 to balance magnitudes
We apply InfSplign on top of SD v1.4 and v2.1 models (Rombach et al., 2022) for 50 inference steps
This results in 3160 prompts that still cover all objects while keeping the dataset size manageable for ablations.
quotes.supports: unseen: tuning subset covers all objects

quotes.text: The optimal values obtained from this study are subsequently used for the experiments on the complete VISOR benchmark
quotes.supports: unseen: tuned values scored on full VISOR
headline: 45.10 on SDXL with no loss
